etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English fort, from Middle French fort (“strong”) (adjective use is from Old French). Doublet of fortis and forte.

definitions.definition: A fortified defensive structure stationed with troops.
(historical) An outlying trading-station, as in British North America.
A structure improvised from furniture, bedding, etc., for playing games.
To create a fort, fortifications, a strong point, or a redoubt.
